In summary, our research is concerned with
the thermodynamic characterization of the electron transfer reactions in proteins.

the evaluation of charge transfer entropics for redox couples and the use of these values to determine the charge transfer entropic contribution to the thermodynamic parameters of electron transfer reactions.
the evaluation of the thermodynamic properties of electron transfer reactions in aqueous buffers and the use of these data in the study of protein redox chemistry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the entropies of charge transfer for the cytochromes c are not the same as those for the redox mediates, and that they are not the same for different proteins.
the charge transfer entropy of the cytochrome oxidoreductase couple in aqueous buffer at 298 degrees k is -16 cal/deg K mol.

the entropic contribution to the reversible electrode potential for a redox reaction in aqueous buffers is dependent upon the structure of both the protein and the redox mediator and that this contribution is not constant but varies from approximately -13 to -44 cal/degrees K. mol for the reactions studied.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the charge transfer entropy is a function of the structure of the reactant and the medium.
the charge transfer entropy of the cytochrome redox couple is -16 +/- 3 cal/degrees K/mol.
the entropy of the cytochrome redox couple is about the same as that for a series of organic dicarboxylate redox couples and about 10 times greater than that for the [Fe (CN)6]3-/4- redox couple.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the entropic contribution to the free energy of a redox reaction is not constant and depends upon the structure of both the electron donor and the electron acceptor.

the charge transfer enthalpies of the redox reactions of the redox proteins are not significantly altered in the redox reactions with the organic and inorganic mediators, whereas the charge transfer entropic changes are large and can be as high as -43 cal/degrees K/mol.
the charge transfer entropy of the cytochrome-c redox couple is -16 cal K-1 mol-1.
